=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Issues Review (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope:** This review is based on the Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA clause text, so the drafting points below need checking against the mark-up. Australian tax, privacy and NSW limitation points should be confirmed by specialists.

**Headline:** The known quantified items total about AUD 4.13m before on-costs: Riverlark ~3.2m, Sandbar 0.33m, bonuses 0.42m and Ironquay 0.18m. Because the Seller discloses these matters and the buyer-knowledge clause excludes them, the buyer cannot rely on warranty claims to recover them. They must be handled through price or debt adjustments, the funds flow, conditions precedent or specific indemnities.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap on general warranty claims at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A materially higher cap, such as 50% of price for general warranties, with fundamental and tax claims carved out (see N-004 and N-016).
- **Recommendation: Reject / counter.** A 20% cap is low for a AUD 24m deal with several known exposures.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** Claims must exceed AUD 25,000 each (de minimis). Aggregate claims must exceed AUD 250,000 before recovery, and only the excess is recoverable (a deductible, about 1% of price).
- **Buyer wants:** A tipping basket (once exceeded, all losses are recoverable), a de minimis of about AUD 10,000, and aggregation of related claims so the threshold is not evaded.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Propose a tipping basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%) with a AUD 10,000 de minimis, because a deductible structure would leave most mid-sized claims unrecoverable.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion. Any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 to 36 months for general warranties, a longer period for tax (at least the ATO amendment period plus notification time), and a separate, longer period for fundamental warranties (see N-004).
- **Recommendation: Reject.** 18 months is too short for an operating business whose tax and IP exposures may only surface at audit or on enforcement.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency) capped at 100% of price, outside the de minimis and basket, with a limitation period of at least six years.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title is the core of what the buyer is paying for and should not sit under general limits "for administrative simplicity."

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** The Seller's update is silent on fraud. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations to "all Claims of any nature," which would also cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express clause stating that nothing limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or dishonesty.
- **Recommendation: Insert.** Australian courts are generally unwilling to enforce exclusions for a party's own fraud, but an express carve-out avoids a costly dispute.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (to 5pm 22 September 2026), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with fair-disclosure standards (sufficient detail for a buyer to understand the matter). No general data room or public record disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Blanket disclosure of the entire data room would hollow out every warranty and undermine the buyer's position.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter known to the buyer or its advisers, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion, plus an express pro-sandbagging clause confirming that the buyer's knowledge does not affect its rights. Known issues are dealt with through specific indemnities and price.
- **Recommendation: Reject and insert pro-sandbagging wording.** Australian law on sandbagging is not settled, so the right should be stated expressly.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** The update says the consent is "addressed" and will be treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent, with reasonable endeavours. The Disclosure Letter says no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions (cl. 11.2 and 11.3) is in the data room. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen's written, unconditional consent as a condition precedent to Completion, with evidence that the 11.3 conditions are met. Only the buyer may waive it. If it is not obtained, the buyer may terminate or take a price adjustment or escrow.
- **Recommendation: Reject reasonable endeavours.** Make the consent a hard condition precedent, since loss of 30% of revenue is a value issue, not a warranty claim.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. The release will be provided after Completion. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is in the data room (cl. 8.1 and 9.2).
- **Buyer wants:** A payout letter, funds flow deduction of the full amount from the price, and executed discharge of security delivered at Completion. The debt-free baseline requires this.
- **Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release.** The buyer should not be left holding a secured facility it has paid for.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses sits outside the funds flow. The Seller says these are its matter. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, with all on-costs, treated as Seller transaction costs or debt-like items and deducted from price. Specific indemnity for any claims by employees under the bonus arrangements.
- **Recommendation: Reprice.** Include the bonuses and quantified on-costs in the funds flow, because they are a pre-Completion liability that would otherwise pass to the buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is described as adequate. DD-004 transfers SOW3 Project Materials only on payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is open per DD-010 (not independently verified), and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Seller to pay all open SOW3 fees before Completion. A confirmatory assignment as a condition precedent. A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay IP ownership and transfer defects, not limited to SOW3, outside the cap and basket.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The indemnity does not match the chain-of-title risk, which goes to the ownership of IP the business uses.

### SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 shows a download link sent to an unintended external address, possibly exposing ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligations are unresolved. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of a forensic investigation and privacy assessment before signing. Notification obligations under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) to be checked and any required steps taken pre-Completion. Specific indemnity for investigation, notification, regulatory, remediation and third-party costs, outside the cap, basket and time limits. Consider an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus escrow.** The incident is unresolved and the disclosure does not quantify it, so the buyer should not rely on the Seller's materiality view.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total), described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Evidence of whether each renewal is terminable or unavoidable and what period it covers. Any pre-Completion portion treated as a debt-like or working capital item. Renewals treated as one matter, so each sits above the de minimis and cannot be split to avoid thresholds.
- **Recommendation: Reject the characterisation.** Require analysis before accepting "ordinary course," and adjust price for any committed amounts that relate to pre-Completion periods.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims of any nature. No separate regimes.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental and title, (c) tax, (d) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Sandbar) and (e) fraud, each with its own cap, threshold and time limit.
- **Recommendation: Insert separate regimes.** A single regime is the mechanism by which the Seller's other positions would neutralise the buyer's protections.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares is evidenced by the share register (DD-012) showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder. The disclosure notes the buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: ASIC company extract, inspection of the original share register and any certificates, a chain-of-title review, a PPSR search for encumbrances, and confirmation of no options, pre-emption rights or other interests over the shares. Signed transfer documents delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Verify independently.** The register alone is only the Seller's own record, and title is the core of the deal.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime" (i.e. N-001 to N-003 limits). No disclosure against either is made.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, uncapped or capped at price, with a time limit matching the ATO amendment period plus time for notification. IP warranties on ownership, chain of title and non-infringement, with the same protections as fundamental warranties.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Tax and IP exposures can crystallise long after the general limits expire, so the general regime cannot apply to them.

---

**Next steps:** (1) Mark up the SPA to reflect N-001 to N-016, prioritising the Bluefen condition, Riverlark payout, bonus funds-flow treatment and the Ironquay and incident indemnities. (2) Commission the title searches and the incident forensic review. (3) Ask the Seller to correct the inconsistency between the Update ("addressed" consent) and the Disclosure Letter (no consent). (4) Have NSW counsel and tax and privacy specialists confirm the drafting.
